tools.name: current_time
tools.description: Returns the exact current date, time, weekday and UTC offset in any time zone. Use this whenever you need to know today's date or the current time instead of guessing — your training data does not know what day it is.

tools.name: convert_timezone
tools.description: Converts a date/time from one time zone to another, correctly handling daylight saving time. If the input already includes an offset or 'Z', from_timezone is ignored.

tools.name: date_add
tools.description: Adds or subtracts a duration (years, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds) to a date/time. Use negative numbers to subtract. Calendar-aware: adding 1 month to Jan 31 gives Feb 28/29, and adding days keeps the same local clock time across daylight-saving changes.

tools.name: date_diff
tools.description: Calculates the exact time between two dates/times: a calendar breakdown (years, months, days, hours, minutes, seconds) plus totals in days, hours, minutes and seconds, and the number of calendar days. Negative if end is before start.

tools.name: business_days
tools.description: Works with business (working) days. mode "add": returns the date N business days after start_date (start_date itself is not counted; negative N goes backward; 0 returns start_date, or the next business day if start_date is not one). mode "count": counts business days from start_date to end_date, inc

tools.name: calculate
tools.description: Evaluates an arithmetic expression exactly, so you don't have to do mental math. Supports + - * / % ^ (or **), parentheses, constants pi/e/tau and functions: sqrt, cbrt, abs, round(x, digits), floor, ceil, trunc, sign, ln, log(x[, base]), log10, log2, exp, pow, sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2

tools.name: convert_units
tools.description: Converts a value between units of length, mass, volume (US and imperial), area, speed, time, digital data (KB vs KiB, bits vs bytes), energy, pressure and temperature. Accepts common abbreviations (km, lb, fl oz, mph, °F, GiB). US customary units are used for cup/pint/quart/gallon unless you say imp

tools.name: text_stats
tools.description: Counts exactly what language models are bad at counting: characters (as humans see them), words, lines, sentences, paragraphs, UTF-8 bytes, and occurrences of a letter or substring (e.g. how many "r" in "strawberry"). Use it to check length limits (tweets, SMS, meta descriptions, form fields) before

tools.name: hash_text
tools.description: Computes a cryptographic hash (SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512) of text, or encodes/decodes it as Base64, Base64URL, hex or URL-encoding. Text is treated as UTF-8.

tools.name: regex_test
tools.description: Runs a JavaScript regular expression against text and returns every match with its position and capture groups, or the text after replacement. Use it to verify a regex actually works before relying on it.

tools.name: validate_email
tools.description: Checks whether an email address is correctly formatted and returns a normalized version. Set check_dns=true to also confirm the domain exists and can receive mail (MX records). Does not send email and cannot confirm that a specific mailbox exists.

tools.name: validate_phone
tools.description: Validates a phone number using Google's libphonenumber rules and returns it in E.164 (+14155552671), international and national formats, plus the country and line type (mobile, fixed line, toll free...). For numbers without a +country code, pass default_country.

tools.name: validate_url
tools.description: Checks that a URL is well-formed, normalizes it (lowercase host, punycode, default ports removed, spaces encoded) and splits it into parts including each query parameter. Flags common problems such as missing scheme, private/localhost addresses and credentials embedded in the URL. Does not fetch the

tools.name: validate_iban
tools.description: Validates an International Bank Account Number: country, length for that country, and the mod-97 check digits. Returns electronic and printed formats. A valid IBAN is correctly formed; this does not confirm the account exists.

tools.name: json_repair
tools.description: Turns almost-JSON into valid JSON: removes markdown code fences, comments and trailing commas, adds missing quotes, commas and closing brackets, converts single quotes, Python True/False/None and truncated output. Returns the repaired JSON string and whether the input was already valid.

tools.name: json_schema_validate
tools.description: Checks a JSON value against a JSON Schema (drafts 4, 7, 2019-09 and 2020-12) and lists every violation with its location. Use it to confirm structured output or an API payload is correct before sending it. `data` and `schema` may be JSON values or JSON strings.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "validate_url" references sensitive artifacts (credentials). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Checks that a URL is well-formed, normalizes it (lowercase host, punycode, default ports removed, spaces encoded) and splits it into parts including each query …

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: validate_email, validate_url · Private data: validate_email, validate_url · Public sink: text_stats, validate_email.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: validate_email, validate_url · Private data: validate_email, validate_url · Public sink: text_stats, validate_email

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
